title: Unproven Bridge Message
summary: A message bridge releases escrowed value when a message is processed. Only a message proven under an accepted root may release funds. A message that was never proven must not pay, a processed message must not pay twice, and only the updater may commit or prove a root.

realWorld.incident: Nomad Bridge Replica process(), Ethereum, exploitation from 2022-08-01 21:32 UTC through 2022-08-02 05:49 UTC
realWorld.lossReported: Over $186M in ERC-20 tokens (Coinbase incident analysis, 9 Aug 2022). BlockSec estimated nearly $200M.
realWorld.rootCause: An unproven message reads as root bytes32(0). Replica.initialize pre-approved confirmAt[bytes32(0)] = 1 when the committed root was zero, so acceptableRoot(bytes32(0)) was true and process() released funds for messages that were never proven.
realWorld.note: Minimal reproduction of the zero-root acceptance bug. Re-implemented from the public post-mortems. The DeFiHackLabs PoC is MIT and is cited only; none of its code is copied. No fork and no Replica bytecode.
